"""Chapter 2-4: a sub-agent. The summariser launches a planner when the report gives no follow-up."""

import asyncio
import sys
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path
from typing import ClassVar, Literal

from langchain_core.tools import BaseTool, tool

from featherweight import (
    AgentBase,
    AgentInput,
    AgentOutput,
    AgentRunner,
    Gemini,
    HttpMCPServer,
    ModelSettings,
    Skill,
    SqliteDatabase,
    StdioMCPServer,
    default_db_path,
)


@tool
def minutes_between(start: str, end: str) -> str:
    """The minutes between two timestamps, each written as 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM'."""
    return str(int((datetime.fromisoformat(end) - datetime.fromisoformat(start)).total_seconds() // 60))


class Report(AgentInput):  # what goes in: a typed model, checked before the model is called
    text: str


class Summary(AgentOutput):  # also carries `open_questions: list[str]`
    title: str = ""  # every field has a default: a model that does not know is not forced to invent
    # only these values, or None when the report does not say
    severity: Literal["low", "medium", "high"] | None = None
    service: str | None = None
    impact: str = ""
    duration_minutes: int | None = None
    owner: str | None = None  # new: the answer of the MCP server
    next_steps: list[str] = []


class Impact(AgentInput):
    impact: str


class Plan(AgentOutput):
    steps: list[str] = []


class ActionPlanner(AgentBase):  # the sub-agent: an agent like any other
    name: str = "action_planner"
    description: str = "Proposes two or three next steps for an incident, from its impact"
    version: str = "1"  # change it when the prompt or the behaviour changes: runs are told apart by it
    prompt: str = "Propose two or three concrete next steps for the incident."
    # the model is a setting of the agent
    model: ModelSettings = Gemini(model="gemini-3.5-flash-lite", thinking="low")
    input_model: ClassVar[type[AgentInput]] = Impact  # the contract is set on the class: the same for every run
    output_model: ClassVar[type[AgentOutput]] = Plan


class IncidentSummariser(AgentBase):
    name: str = "incident_summariser"  # how the run log and the traces name the agent
    description: str = "Turns an incident report into a short, structured summary"
    version: str = "5"  # change it when the prompt or the behaviour changes: runs are told apart by it
    prompt: str = (
        "Summarise the incident report. Use only what the report says. "
        "If the severity is not stated, decide it with your skill. If the service is not stated, leave it out and ask in open_questions. "
        "If the report gives a start and an end time, use minutes_between for duration_minutes. "
        "If the report names a service, find who owns it with your tools and put the team in owner. "
        "If the report lists no follow-up, launch the action_planner with the impact and use its steps as next_steps."
    )
    # the model is a setting of the agent
    model: ModelSettings = Gemini(model="gemini-3.5-flash-lite", thinking="low")
    skills: list[Skill] = [Skill.from_directory("2-3/severity-rubric")]  # read on demand, not in every prompt
    subagents: list[type] = [ActionPlanner]  # the only agent this one may launch
    tools: list[BaseTool] = [minutes_between]  # an allow-list: only these tools are bound to the model
    mcp_servers: list[StdioMCPServer | HttpMCPServer] = [  # the runner starts this server when the agent needs it
        StdioMCPServer(
            name="services",
            command=sys.executable,
            args=("services_server.py",),
            description="Who owns a service, and who is on call",
        )
    ]
    input_model: ClassVar[type[AgentInput]] = Report  # the contract is set on the class: the same for every run
    output_model: ClassVar[type[AgentOutput]] = Summary

    def check_output(self, agent_input, output):  # a rule the schema cannot say: raise to reject the attempt
        if output.service and output.service.lower() not in agent_input.text.lower():
            raise ValueError(f"The report does not name the service {output.service!r}")


async def main(path: str = "reports/02-sign-in-trouble.txt") -> None:
    report = Report(text=Path(path).read_text())
    async with SqliteDatabase(default_db_path()) as db:
        job_id = await db.create_job("incident-report")  # a job id groups the runs of one piece of work
        # the class, not an instance: the runner builds the agent
        result = await AgentRunner(db).run(IncidentSummariser, report, job_id=job_id)
    print(result.status.value, result.model_name, result.output or result.error)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main(*sys.argv[1:2]))

Run it with make book-chapter N=2-4. It reads reports/02-sign-in-trouble.txt, which lists no follow-up. Something like:

SUCCESS gemini-3.5-flash-lite open_questions=[...] title='Sign-in trouble' severity='medium' ... next_steps=['Find the cause in the server logs', 'Add an alert on blank sign-in pages']

What to notice

  • ActionPlanner is an ordinary agent, with its own input and output models. Nothing marks it as a sub-agent.
  • subagents is an allow-list of classes. The agent can launch exactly these. The prompt lists them, and the runner gives the agent two tools: get_agent_schema and launch_agent. launch_agent waits for the child and returns its output as text. See launching agents.
  • The child is a run of its own, with its own rows in the run log, linked to the parent's.
  • Limits keep a chain from running away: how deep agents may launch agents, and how many launches one attempt may make. They are in the guide; nothing to set for this example.
  • A launched child blocks its parent. For work that goes on while the agent carries on, see background jobs.

Why an allow-list of classes. There is no registry to maintain, and an agent can launch only what it declares. See launching agents.

Also possible

  • How deep, and how many, agents may launch agents: the limits.
  • A sub-agent on an allow-list: the recipe.
  • Give it what the parent knows: a context field in its input.

Next: Part 3 adds jobs to the assistant, to run it over many reports.

docs.title: What a job is
docs.text:
Turn the agent's work into a job: a declared class that you run with run_job.

This part adds jobs to the assistant from Part 1; you can read it without the other parts. incident.py in each folder is that assistant, unchanged: its models and its agent. The new code is only the jobs.

"""Chapter 3-1: a job is a declared class: one that summarises a report, and one that runs the assistant over many."""

import asyncio
from pathlib import Path

from incident import IncidentSummariser, Report, Summary
from pydantic import BaseModel

from featherweight import AgentRunner, JobContext, SqliteDatabase, job, run_job


@job  # a class made from this function: a name, a version, a typed input and output
async def summarise(ctx: JobContext, input: Report) -> Summary:
    result = await ctx.run(IncidentSummariser, input)  # a run of an agent, inside the job
    if result.output is None:
        raise RuntimeError(result.error)
    return result.output


class Reports(BaseModel):
    paths: list[str]


class Digest(BaseModel):
    summaries: list[Summary]


@job  # a class made from this function: a name, a version, a typed input and output
async def summarise_all(ctx: JobContext, input: Reports) -> Digest:
    reports = [Report(text=Path(path).read_text()) for path in input.paths]
    results = await ctx.run_many(IncidentSummariser, reports)  # all at once, in order
    failed = [path for path, result in zip(input.paths, results, strict=True) if result.output is None]
    if failed:  # a digest with gaps would look complete: fail, and say which reports
        raise RuntimeError(f"Could not summarise: {', '.join(failed)}")
    return Digest(summaries=[r.output for r in results if r.output])


async def main() -> None:
    async with SqliteDatabase(":memory:") as db:  # no file: a quick try
        runner = AgentRunner(db)
        one = await run_job(runner, summarise, Report(text=Path("reports/01-checkout-outage.txt").read_text()))
        print(one.status.value, one.result.title if one.result else one.error)
        paths = sorted(str(p) for p in Path("reports").glob("*.txt"))
        many = await run_job(runner, summarise_all, Reports(paths=paths))
        print(many.status.value, [s.title for s in many.result.summaries] if many.result else many.error)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())

Run it: make book-chapter N=3-1

SUCCESS Checkout was down
SUCCESS ['Checkout was down', 'Sign-in trouble', 'Search was slow', 'Batch was late']

What to notice

  • A job is a function with a typed input and a typed output. @job turns it into a class with a name, a version and the two models, and run_job runs it and returns an outcome: status, result (the output model) and error. A job that fails is an outcome, not an exception, as for a run.
  • ctx.run and ctx.run_many run agents in the job. They share the job's id, so the runs are recorded under it (the next chapter).
  • The pipeline is plain Python. summarise_all reads files and collects results with a list comprehension: no graph, no special syntax.
  • SqliteDatabase(":memory:") keeps the run log in memory: a quick try with no file, gone when the program ends.
  • When to use a job. Use one when the work is something you want to name, follow, run again or hand to someone else: it spans several runs, an API triggers it, or it can fail halfway and should pick up again. A single agent call in a script needs no job: runner.run is enough.
  • What a job gives you that a function does not. A name and a version, so a change is visible; a status, events and a run log you can read; its output in a store you choose; resume after a failure; and the same job on a worker, with no rewrite.

Why a class. A declared job has a name, a version and typed models, so the same job can be run here (run_job) or on a worker (Part 5), and be told apart when it changes. See the philosophy, the job, running a job class and the guide.

Also possible

  • An agent is a job too: pass it to run_job or submit as it is. See the jobs guide.
  • A pipeline of two agents, in plain Python.

Follow a job through its status and its events.

"""Chapter 3-2: a job has a status and events, and its runs are in the run log."""

import asyncio
from pathlib import Path

from incident import IncidentSummariser, Report, Summary
from pydantic import BaseModel

from featherweight import AgentRunner, JobContext, SqliteDatabase, default_db_path, job, run_job


class Reports(BaseModel):
    paths: list[str]


class Digest(BaseModel):
    summaries: list[Summary]


@job  # a class made from this function: a name, a version, a typed input and output
async def summarise_all(ctx: JobContext, input: Reports) -> Digest:
    reports = [Report(text=Path(path).read_text()) for path in input.paths]
    results = await ctx.run_many(IncidentSummariser, reports)
    failed = [path for path, result in zip(input.paths, results, strict=True) if result.output is None]
    if failed:  # a digest with gaps would look complete: fail, and say which reports
        raise RuntimeError(f"Could not summarise: {', '.join(failed)}")
    return Digest(summaries=[r.output for r in results if r.output])


async def main() -> None:
    paths = sorted(str(p) for p in Path("reports").glob("*.txt"))
    async with SqliteDatabase(default_db_path()) as db:
        outcome = await run_job(AgentRunner(db), summarise_all, Reports(paths=paths))
        job_row = await db.get_job(outcome.job_id)
        assert job_row  # the job is there
        print("job:", job_row.name, job_row.status.value, f"version {job_row.job_version}")
        print("events:", [event.type for event in await db.list_job_events(outcome.job_id)])
        for attempt in await db.list_attempts(job_id=outcome.job_id):  # one row for each attempt of each run
            print(
                f"  {attempt.agent_name} attempt {attempt.attempt}: {attempt.status.value}, tokens={attempt.input_tokens}+{attempt.output_tokens}"
            )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())

Run it: make book-chapter N=3-2

job: summarise_all SUCCESS version 1
events: ['queued', 'running', 'succeeded']
  incident_summariser attempt 1: SUCCESS, tokens=312+96
  ... (one row for each report)

What to notice

  • The job row has its name, its status and its version. Reading it is db.get_job(job_id).
  • Events are the history of the job's status, one for each change: queued, running, then succeeded or failed. The database writes each event in the same step as the change, so they cannot disagree. A client in another process follows them as a stream (Part 5).
  • The run log (db.list_attempts(job_id=...)) has one row for each attempt of each run in the job: status, model, tokens, time and hashes.
  • Metadata and nothing else. No report, no summary and no error text is in any of it: the framework stores metadata, and you bring the storage.

Why metadata. What went through the job is yours, and so is how it is kept. See the rule and job events.

Next: where the job's output goes.

docs.title: Results and the result store
docs.text:
Keep what a job produced in a result store that you own.

"""Chapter 3-3: the job's output goes to the result store that you choose; featherweight keeps no results of its own."""

import asyncio
from pathlib import Path

from incident import IncidentSummariser, Report, Summary

from featherweight import AgentRunner, JobContext, ResultKey, SqliteDatabase, SqliteResultStore, job, run_job


@job  # a class made from this function: a name, a version, a typed input and output
async def summarise(ctx: JobContext, input: Report) -> Summary:
    result = await ctx.run(IncidentSummariser, input)
    if result.output is None:
        raise RuntimeError(result.error)
    return result.output


async def main() -> None:
    report = Report(text=Path("reports/01-checkout-outage.txt").read_text())
    async with SqliteDatabase(":memory:") as db:
        store = SqliteResultStore(db)  # a result store of ours: a sqlite one, for local work. Yours goes here
        outcome = await run_job(AgentRunner(db, results=store), summarise, report)
        print("returned:", outcome.result.title if outcome.result else outcome.error)

        row = await db.get_job(outcome.job_id)
        assert row and row.job_hash and row.input_hash  # a job class has both hashes
        # the key of a stored result: the job's id, the job's hash (the field is called agent_hash) and the input's hash
        key = ResultKey(job_id=outcome.job_id, agent_hash=row.job_hash, input_hash=row.input_hash)
        print("in the store:", await store.get(key))  # what a later reader finds: Part 5's client does this for you

        outcome = await run_job(AgentRunner(db, results=None), summarise, report)  # no store: nothing is kept
        print("results=None, still returned:", outcome.result is not None)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())

Run it: make book-chapter N=3-3

returned: Checkout was down
in the store: {'open_questions': [], 'title': 'Checkout was down', 'severity': 'high', ...}
results=None, still returned: True

What to notice

  • run_job returns the output, and also writes it to the runner's result store, if the runner has one. The store is a results= argument.
  • SqliteResultStore is for local work: it keeps results in the same sqlite file as the run log. In a deployment the store is yours: a bucket, a table, a database for each customer. Part 6 writes one.
  • A later reader gets it from the store, by key: the job's id, the job's hash and the input's hash. In Part 5 a client does this for you and parses it into the job's output model.
  • results=None keeps nothing. The outcome still has the output, but it is gone when the program ends, and there is nothing for a later job to resume from.

Why no results of our own. Results are application data, so you decide where they live. See the rule and the result store.

docs.title: Resume
docs.text:
Run a failed job again without paying for the steps that worked.

"""Chapter 3-4: a resumable job that dies after its summaries, and a second job that resumes it."""

import asyncio
from pathlib import Path

from incident import IncidentSummariser, Report, Summary
from pydantic import BaseModel

from featherweight import AgentRunner, JobContext, SqliteDatabase, job, run_job

RANK = {"high": 0, "medium": 1, "low": 2, None: 3}  # most severe first; no severity last


class Reports(BaseModel):
    paths: list[str]
    crash: bool = False  # to show a failure: the job dies after the summaries


class Digest(BaseModel):
    summaries: list[Summary]


@job  # a class made from this function: a name, a version, a typed input and output
async def summarise_all(ctx: JobContext, input: Reports) -> Digest:
    reports = [Report(text=Path(path).read_text()) for path in input.paths]
    results = await ctx.run_many(IncidentSummariser, reports)
    failed = [path for path, result in zip(input.paths, results, strict=True) if result.output is None]
    if failed:  # a digest with gaps would look complete: fail, and say which reports
        raise RuntimeError(f"Could not summarise: {', '.join(failed)}")
    if input.crash:
        raise RuntimeError("simulated crash: the process died after the summaries")
    summaries: list[Summary] = [r.output for r in results if r.output]
    summaries.sort(key=lambda s: RANK[s.severity])  # plain Python, the same each time
    return Digest(summaries=summaries)


async def show(db, label: str, job_id: str) -> None:
    print(label)
    for attempt in await db.list_attempts(job_id=job_id):
        print(
            f"  {attempt.status.value:<8} {'reused: no model call' if attempt.reused_from_attempt_id else 'model call'}"
        )


async def main() -> None:
    paths = sorted(str(p) for p in Path("reports").glob("*.txt"))
    async with SqliteDatabase(":memory:") as db:
        runner = AgentRunner(db)
        # resumable: keep the results of the steps, so that a later job can resume from this one
        first = await run_job(runner, summarise_all, Reports(paths=paths, crash=True), resumable=True)
        print("first:", first.status.value, first.error)
        await show(db, "first run", first.job_id)
        # a new job: the steps that finished are not run again
        second = await run_job(runner, summarise_all, Reports(paths=paths), resume_from=first.job_id)
        print("second:", second.status.value)
        await show(db, "second run", second.job_id)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())

Run it: make book-chapter N=3-4. The first run fails on purpose, and featherweight logs that failure, with its traceback, to stderr: that is expected.

first: FAILED RuntimeError: simulated crash: the process died after the summaries
first run
  SUCCESS  model call
  ... (four runs)
second: SUCCESS
second run
  SUCCESS  reused: no model call
  ... (four runs)

What to notice

  • resumable=True is decided before the job runs: it keeps the output of each step in the result store, so that a later job can use it. A job that did not keep them cannot be resumed.
  • resume_from=first.job_id starts a new job that points to the failed one. The runs that already succeeded, with the same agent and the same input, are answered from the kept results: no model call, no tokens. The failed job stays as a record.
  • The code between the agents must give the same inputs each time, which is why the digest is sorted with plain, deterministic Python. If the code took another path, the inputs would differ and the agents would run again.
  • The crash is simulated with a flag in the input. In real life it is a process that dies or a step that raises.

Why a new job. A resume is you running a job that ended again, so it is its own job with its own trace. See resuming a job and the resume example.

Also possible

  • Resuming a failed job, as a recipe.

docs.text:
Turn the assistant into a chat that streams its answer.

This part adds a chat to the assistant from Part 1. You can read it without the other parts.

"""Chapter 4-1: a chat that streams its answer. The report is the first message of the conversation."""

import asyncio
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from ag_ui.core import TextMessageContentEvent
from langchain_core.messages import AIMessage, BaseMessage, HumanMessage

from featherweight import AgentRunner, ChatInput, Gemini, ModelSettings, SqliteDatabase, StreamingAgent, default_db_path


class IncidentAssistant(StreamingAgent):  # a streaming agent answers in a chat: no output model, no retries
    name: str = "incident_assistant"
    description: str = "Answers questions about an incident report"
    version: str = "1"  # change it when the prompt or the behaviour changes: runs are told apart by it
    prompt: str = (
        "The first message is an incident report. Answer questions about it in a sentence or two, only from the report."
    )
    # the model is a setting of the agent
    model: ModelSettings = Gemini(model="gemini-3.5-flash-lite", thinking="low")


async def read_line(prompt: str) -> str:  # the event loop reads the terminal, so that Control-C can leave
    loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
    line: asyncio.Future[str] = loop.create_future()
    print(prompt, end="", flush=True)
    loop.add_reader(sys.stdin, lambda: line.set_result(sys.stdin.readline().strip()))
    try:
        return await line
    finally:
        loop.remove_reader(sys.stdin)


async def main(path: str = "reports/01-checkout-outage.txt") -> None:
    greeting = "I have the report. Ask me anything about it."
    history: list[BaseMessage] = [HumanMessage(Path(path).read_text()), AIMessage(greeting)]  # featherweight keeps none
    print(greeting)
    async with SqliteDatabase(default_db_path()) as db, AgentRunner(db) as runner:
        while text := await read_line("\nyou> "):  # an empty line leaves
            user = HumanMessage(text)
            # the conversation is yours: the whole history goes in at each turn
            run = runner.stream(IncidentAssistant, ChatInput.from_langchain([*history, user]))
            async for event in run:
                if isinstance(event, TextMessageContentEvent):
                    print(event.delta, end="", flush=True)  # the answer, as the model writes it
            history += [user, *run.new_messages]  # what was said, for the next turn


if __name__ == "__main__":
    try:
        asyncio.run(main(*sys.argv[1:2]))
    except (KeyboardInterrupt, EOFError):
        pass

Run it, and type a question about the report. An empty line, or Control-C, leaves.

make book-chapter N=4-1

I have the report. Ask me anything about it.

you> why did checkout fail?
A new release of the payment form sent a field the provider rejects, so every payment failed.

(The plain command is docker compose run --rm --no-deps book python 4-1/app.py, from docs/book/code: see the container.)

What to notice

  • A streaming agent is declared like an agent, with no output_model. Nothing is validated at the end, and a failed turn is not retried: once a word is out, it cannot be taken back.
  • runner.stream(...) gives events, not a result. You print each TextMessageContentEvent.delta as it arrives.
  • You keep the conversation. featherweight stores no conversations: run.new_messages is what the agent said and did this turn, and you add it to your own history.
  • The report is the first message, followed by a short greeting from the assistant so the roles alternate, which providers expect.
  • read_line reads the terminal through the event loop. A thread stuck in input() would keep the process alive after Control-C.

Why events. A chat has no finished output to check, so the answer is a stream a person reads as it is written. See streaming agents and the spec.

To send the assistant a file with a question, see Attaching a file.

Also possible

  • Show the model's thoughts: show_thoughts, in Thoughts.

Send the stream to a browser with AG-UI or the Vercel AI SDK.

"""Chapter 4-2: the same assistant behind a web API, for a browser to talk to."""

from contextlib import asynccontextmanager

from fastapi import FastAPI, Request
from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse, StreamingResponse

from featherweight import (
    AgentRunner,
    AttachmentLimitError,
    BadRequest,
    Gemini,
    ModelSettings,
    SqliteDatabase,
    StreamingAgent,
    default_db_path,
)
from featherweight.adapters import agui, vercel


class IncidentAssistant(StreamingAgent):  # a streaming agent answers in a chat: no output model, no retries
    name: str = "incident_assistant"
    description: str = "Answers questions about an incident report"
    version: str = "1"  # change it when the prompt or the behaviour changes: runs are told apart by it
    prompt: str = (
        "The first message is an incident report. Answer questions about it in a sentence or two, only from the report."
    )
    # the model is a setting of the agent
    model: ModelSettings = Gemini(model="gemini-3.5-flash-lite", thinking="low")


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI):
    async with SqliteDatabase(default_db_path()) as db, AgentRunner(db) as app.state.runner:
        yield


app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)


@app.exception_handler(AttachmentLimitError)
async def too_many_files(request: Request, exc: AttachmentLimitError):
    return JSONResponse({"error": str(exc)}, status_code=413)  # more files, or more bytes, than the agent allows


@app.exception_handler(BadRequest)
async def bad_request(request: Request, exc: BadRequest):
    return JSONResponse({"error": str(exc)}, status_code=422)  # a body that is not a chat request


@app.post("/vercel")  # the Vercel AI SDK: useChat
async def vercel_chat(request: Request):
    run = request.app.state.runner.stream(IncidentAssistant, vercel.parse_request(await request.body()))
    return StreamingResponse(vercel.encode(run), headers=vercel.HEADERS)


@app.post("/agui")  # an AG-UI client
async def agui_chat(request: Request):
    run = request.app.state.runner.stream(IncidentAssistant, agui.parse_request(await request.body()))
    return StreamingResponse(agui.encode(run), headers=agui.HEADERS, media_type=agui.CONTENT_TYPE)

featherweight runs no server. The adapters read a request and turn the events into the stream a client expects, and your web framework sends them: here FastAPI, which is not in the book's image, so install it where you run the server. In the container (this also publishes the port, which the book's container does not do by default):

docker compose run --rm --no-deps -p 8000:8000 book \
  sh -c "pip install -q fastapi uvicorn && python -m uvicorn --app-dir 4-2 app:app --host 0.0.0.0"

Without Docker: pip install fastapi uvicorn, then uvicorn --app-dir 4-2 app:app.

What to notice

  • Two endpoints, one agent. /vercel speaks the Vercel AI SDK stream, and /agui speaks AG-UI. parse_request reads the client's conversation, and encode writes the events.
  • The client sends the whole conversation, report included, on every request. The server keeps nothing.
  • A body that is not a chat request is a BadRequest: answer it with a 422, as the handler does. A conversation with more files, or more bytes, than the agent allows is an AttachmentLimitError, which is a BadRequest too: runner.stream() raises it, and the handler for the subclass answers it with a 413 first. See Attaching a file.

A browser using the Vercel AI SDK's useChat hook posts to /vercel. This is a sketch of the client, not run in the book (the SDK's API changes between versions: check yours):

const { messages, sendMessage, stop } = useChat({
  transport: new DefaultChatTransport({ api: "http://localhost:8000/vercel" }),
});

The first message the page sends is the report, and the following ones are questions. stop() is the next chapter.

Why adapters. The events are one protocol, AG-UI, and each client's format is a translation at the edge. See the spec.

Also possible

  • A chat that streams, keeping the conversation yourself.

Next: stopping a response, and keeping the conversation.

docs.title: Stopping and the conversation
docs.text:
Stop an answer midway, and keep the conversation in a file you own.

"""Chapter 4-3: Control-C stops an answer, and the conversation is kept in a file that you own."""

import asyncio
import json
import signal
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from ag_ui.core import TextMessageContentEvent
from langchain_core.messages import AIMessage, BaseMessage, HumanMessage, messages_from_dict, messages_to_dict

from featherweight import AgentRunner, ChatInput, Gemini, ModelSettings, SqliteDatabase, StreamingAgent, default_db_path

SAVED = default_db_path().with_name("chat.json")  # next to the run log: /data/chat.json in the container


class IncidentAssistant(StreamingAgent):  # a streaming agent answers in a chat: no output model, no retries
    name: str = "incident_assistant"
    description: str = "Answers questions about an incident report"
    version: str = "1"  # change it when the prompt or the behaviour changes: runs are told apart by it
    prompt: str = (
        "The first message is an incident report. Answer questions about it in a sentence or two, only from the report."
    )
    # the model is a setting of the agent
    model: ModelSettings = Gemini(model="gemini-3.5-flash-lite", thinking="low")


async def read_line(prompt: str) -> str:  # the event loop reads the terminal, so that Control-C can leave
    loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
    line: asyncio.Future[str] = loop.create_future()
    print(prompt, end="", flush=True)
    loop.add_reader(sys.stdin, lambda: line.set_result(sys.stdin.readline().strip()))
    try:
        return await line
    finally:
        loop.remove_reader(sys.stdin)


async def main(path: str = "reports/01-checkout-outage.txt") -> None:
    history: list[BaseMessage]
    if SAVED.exists():
        history = messages_from_dict(json.loads(SAVED.read_text()))
    else:
        history = [HumanMessage(Path(path).read_text()), AIMessage("I have the report. Ask me anything about it.")]
    loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
    async with SqliteDatabase(default_db_path()) as db, AgentRunner(db) as runner:
        while text := await read_line("\nyou> "):  # Control-C here leaves; an empty line leaves too
            user = HumanMessage(text)
            # the conversation is yours: the whole history goes in at each turn
            run = runner.stream(IncidentAssistant, ChatInput.from_langchain([*history, user]))
            loop.add_signal_handler(signal.SIGINT, run.cancel)  # Control-C while it answers stops the answer
            async for event in run:
                if isinstance(event, TextMessageContentEvent):
                    print(event.delta, end="", flush=True)
            loop.remove_signal_handler(signal.SIGINT)
            history += [user, *run.new_messages]  # the partial answer is in it too, if you stopped it
            SAVED.write_text(json.dumps(messages_to_dict(history)))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    try:
        asyncio.run(main(*sys.argv[1:2]))
    except (KeyboardInterrupt, EOFError):
        pass

make book-chapter N=4-3

Ask something, press Control-C while it answers, and ask again: the next turn knows what the assistant had already said. The next run continues from the saved conversation.

What to notice

  • Two meanings of Control-C. While the agent answers, the signal handler calls run.cancel(), which stops the answer. While you are typing, it leaves, because the handler is only installed during a turn.
  • A stopped turn is kept. run.new_messages holds the partial answer, cleaned up (a half-written tool call is dropped, and a tool call that never returned gets a "cancelled" result), so the next request can include it and the provider accepts it.
  • The run is CANCELLED in the run log, as any stopped run is.
  • The history is yours. featherweight keeps no conversation, so the example saves it to chat.json next to the run log, with LangChain's own converters. A database or a cache is the same idea.
  • Over the web, a client that stops (stop() in useChat) drops the stream, and the run stops with it. To stop by id, call runner.cancel(run_id), taking the id from the first event, from your own endpoint: see stopping a response.

Why you keep it. The history belongs to your application and its store, so it is not ours to keep. See keeping the conversation.

Next: send the assistant a file with a question.

docs.title: Attaching a file
docs.text:
Send the assistant a file with a question: a PDF, an image, a recording or a video.

"""Chapter 4-4: attach a file to a message. The file travels with the question, as inline data."""

import asyncio
import base64
import mimetypes
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from ag_ui.core import TextMessageContentEvent
from langchain_core.messages import AIMessage, BaseMessage, HumanMessage

from featherweight import AgentRunner, ChatInput, Gemini, ModelSettings, SqliteDatabase, StreamingAgent, default_db_path


class IncidentAssistant(StreamingAgent):
    name: str = "incident_assistant"
    description: str = "Answers questions about an incident report and the files attached to the chat"
    version: str = "2"  # the prompt changed
    prompt: str = (
        "The first message is an incident report. Answer questions about it in a sentence or two, "
        "from the report and from the files the user attaches."
    )
    model: ModelSettings = Gemini(model="gemini-3.5-flash-lite", thinking="low")
    max_attachments = 3  # the limit is the agent's: ten by default, and 15 MiB in all


def attach(question: str, path: str) -> HumanMessage:
    """A message with a file: its bytes, base64-encoded, and its type. What a user may attach, and reading it, is yours."""
    file = Path(path)
    mime = mimetypes.guess_type(file.name)[0] or "application/octet-stream"
    kind = mime.split("/")[0]
    block = {
        "type": kind if kind in ("image", "audio", "video") else "file",
        "base64": base64.b64encode(file.read_bytes()).decode(),
        "mime_type": mime,
        "filename": file.name,
    }
    return HumanMessage([{"type": "text", "text": question}, block])


async def main(report: str = "reports/01-checkout-outage.txt", runbook: str = "4-4/runbook.pdf") -> None:
    history: list[BaseMessage] = [HumanMessage(Path(report).read_text()), AIMessage("I have the report.")]
    questions = [
        attach("What does the runbook say to do about this?", runbook),
        HumanMessage("And who owns the integration?"),
    ]
    async with SqliteDatabase(default_db_path()) as db, AgentRunner(db) as runner:
        for message in questions:  # the second question has no file: the first one is still in the history
            run = runner.stream(IncidentAssistant, ChatInput.from_langchain([*history, message]))
            async for event in run:
                if isinstance(event, TextMessageContentEvent):
                    print(event.delta, end="", flush=True)
            print()
            history += [message, *run.new_messages]


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main(*sys.argv[1:3]))

make book-chapter N=4-4

The assistant reads 4-4/runbook.pdf with the first question, and answers the second from the conversation, with no file:

Roll back the last release of the payment form, tell the payments team, and post in the incident channel once payments succeed.
The payments team owns the integration with the payment provider.

What to notice

  • The file is a block of the message. attach builds a HumanMessage whose content is a list: the question, then the file as base64 with its mime_type and filename. A PDF is a file block; an image, audio or video is an image, audio or video block.
  • featherweight only passes it on. It reads nothing, converts nothing and fetches nothing, and it does not know what the model can read. If the provider says no (a type it does not accept, a file that is too big), the turn fails with the provider's error, as any failed turn does.
  • Only the bytes are accepted, not a URL. A message with a link in its file block is refused when the ChatInput is built. Download the file yourself, check it as you see fit, and send what you have. The bytes are base64 as base64.b64encode gives it (no data: prefix, no line breaks), and a file with no bytes is refused.
  • The file stays in the history. The second question has no file, and it works because the first message, with its file, is still in history. Every turn sends the whole history again, so a file is sent again, and it counts again.
  • The limits are the agent's. max_attachments is 10 by default and the data may not be over 15 MiB (max_attachments = 0 turns attachments off). Here the agent says 3. Over a limit, runner.stream() raises an AttachmentLimitError before anything runs. It is a BadRequest (and a ValueError), so a web application answers it like one: the handler of chapter 4-2 gives it a 413.
  • Providers differ. Gemini reads all four types, Claude reads images and PDFs, and a provider may drop a type without an error. Check what the providers accept, which is a dated snapshot, and try your type with your model.

Why bytes only. How a file is fetched, scanned and stored is your application's decision, and a URL that a user chose is not one a framework should open for you. See attachments and the spec.

Not a chat? Attachments are a feature of the chat. An agent that a job runs, and a job that waits in a queue, do not carry files, on purpose: they pass a reference (an id for a file that you keep in your own store), and a tool fetches the file and checks who is asking. See files for an agent or a job.

docs.title: Submit and a worker
docs.text:
Submit a job from one process and run it on a worker.

Part 5 takes the assistant into production. It builds on the jobs of Part 3 (digest.py is the job summarise_all from there) and on the chat of Part 4 (chapter 5-3): read those first. Each folder runs on its own.

Until now you ran the job in your own process with run_job. Here a client submits it, and a worker runs it.

"""Chapter 5-1: submit the job, and let a worker run it. They only meet in the queue and the database."""

import asyncio
from pathlib import Path

from digest import Digest, Reports, summarise_all

from featherweight import AgentRunner, JobClient, JobWorker, SqliteDatabase, SqliteQueue, default_db_path


async def main() -> None:
    paths = sorted(str(p) for p in Path("reports").glob("*.txt"))
    async with SqliteDatabase(default_db_path()) as db:
        queue = SqliteQueue(db)  # the queue: sqlite for local work, yours in production (Part 6)
        worker = JobWorker(db, queue, AgentRunner(db), jobs=[summarise_all])  # a worker runs only the jobs you list
        running = asyncio.create_task(worker.run())  # in real life a process of its own: worker.py

        client = JobClient(db, queue)  # the client only writes to the queue and the database
        job_id = await client.submit(summarise_all, Reports(paths=paths))
        async for event in client.events(job_id):  # until the job is final
            print(event.type)  # queued, running, succeeded
        digest = await client.result(summarise_all, job_id)  # read from your result store
        assert isinstance(digest, Digest)  # the job's output model, parsed
        print(len(digest.summaries), "summaries; first:", digest.summaries[0].title)

        await worker.stop()
        await running


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
queued running succeeded 4 summaries; first: something like the most severe report 
As two processes (the container shares the data volume), start the worker in one terminal and submit from another:

<!-- code: code/5-1/worker.py -->
```python
"""Chapter 5-1: the worker as a process of its own. It takes jobs from the queue until it is stopped."""

import asyncio

from digest import summarise_all

from featherweight import AgentRunner, JobWorker, SqliteDatabase, SqliteQueue, default_db_path


async def main() -> None:
    async with SqliteDatabase(default_db_path()) as db:
        # takes jobs from the queue until it is stopped
        await JobWorker(db, SqliteQueue(db), AgentRunner(db), jobs=[summarise_all]).run()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```python


docker compose run --rm --no-deps book python 5-1/worker.py     # terminal 1: runs until you stop it
docker compose run --rm --no-deps book python 5-1/submit.py     # terminal 2

What to notice

  • submit returns at once. The client never runs the job: it writes the job and puts a message on the queue. The worker takes the message and runs it. JobWorker(..., jobs=[summarise_all]) runs only the jobs you list.
  • The client and the worker only meet in the queue and the database, so they can be two processes, or two machines.
  • The result is in your result store. client.result reads the job's output from it. The default is a sqlite store for local work, and Part 6 shows how to bring your own.
  • client.events(job_id) streams the job's status changes until it is final. Over SSE it is sse.encode(client.events(job_id)): see events and SSE.
  • client.cancel(job_id) cancels a queued job at once, and asks a running one to stop.
  • It is the same job as in Part 3. run_job(runner, summarise_all, ...) runs it here, and client.submit(summarise_all, ...) has a worker run it: only who runs it, and where, differs.

Why a queue and a database. Nothing connects the two sides directly, so either can restart or move without the other. featherweight ships a sqlite queue for local work; in production the queue is yours. The database is shared too: SqliteDatabase on one machine, and PostgresDatabase, which ships in the package, across machines (Part 6). See submitted jobs and the guide.

Also possible

  • A worker can find a job that is not in its code: jobs_lookup.
  • A job that a worker runs, as a recipe.

docs.title: Several workers
docs.text:
Run several workers, and lose one without losing the job.

Add as many workers as you like. When one dies, another takes its job.

"""Chapter 5-2: kill a worker in the middle of a job, and another worker takes the job over."""

import asyncio
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

from pydantic import BaseModel

from featherweight import AgentRunner, JobClient, JobContext, JobWorker, SqliteDatabase, SqliteQueue, job

LEASE = 1.0  # seconds: short, so that this takes seconds. The default is 60.
os.environ["FTW_JOB_LEASE"] = os.environ["FTW_QUEUE_LEASE"] = str(
    LEASE
)  # settings are environment variables: a worker process inherits them


class Nap(BaseModel):
    seconds: float


class Rested(BaseModel):
    rested: float


@job(timeout=30)  # a job that runs longer than this fails with JobTimeout
async def nap(ctx: JobContext, input: Nap) -> Rested:  # a stand-in for a long job: it needs no model
    await asyncio.sleep(input.seconds)
    return Rested(rested=input.seconds)


async def worker(path: str) -> None:
    async with SqliteDatabase(path) as db:
        queue = SqliteQueue(db)
        await JobWorker(db, queue, AgentRunner(db), jobs=[nap]).run()


async def main() -> None:
    path = str(Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) / "workers.db")
    async with SqliteDatabase(path) as db:
        client = JobClient(db, SqliteQueue(db))
        a = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, __file__, "worker", path])  # worker A, a process of its own
        job_id = await client.submit(nap, Nap(seconds=2))
        b = None
        async for event in client.events(job_id):
            print(event.type)  # queued, running, lost, running, succeeded
            if event.type == "running" and b is None:
                a.kill()  # SIGKILL: no goodbye, and the lease stops being renewed
                print("worker A killed")
                b = asyncio.create_task(worker(path))  # worker B
        print((await client.status(job_id)).executions, "executions")  # 2
        if b:
            b.cancel()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    if sys.argv[1:2] == ["worker"]:
        asyncio.run(worker(sys.argv[2]))
    else:
        asyncio.run(main())

queued
running
worker A killed
lost
running
succeeded
2 executions

What to notice

  • A lease. While a worker runs a job it renews two leases every third of the job's lease (FTW_JOB_LEASE, 60 seconds by default, 1 here): the job's, in the database, and its message's (FTW_QUEUE_LEASE), in the queue. Settings like these are environment variables, and a worker process inherits them. A worker killed with SIGKILL stops renewing them.
  • A takeover. When the leases run out, the message comes back to a worker, which sees that the job's lease expired and takes the job over. It is the same job with executions one higher, and a lost event in its events.
  • A job must be safe to run twice. A worker that was only paused, and wakes up after a takeover, is refused its writes and stops the job; but what the job's own code already did (a mail sent, an API called) is not undone. A resumable job reuses the steps that finished, as in a resume.
  • timeout. A job that runs longer than its timeout (600 seconds by default) fails with JobTimeout. A heartbeat only shows that a worker is alive, so a hung job needs this.
  • How often a message may come back is your queue's policy; SqliteQueue marks a message dead after FTW_QUEUE_MAX_DELIVERIES (3) deliveries.

Why the same job. The job id is what the client holds: its events, its cancel and its result are all keyed by it, so a takeover keeps it. See several workers and the guide.

Also possible

  • Every setting you can tune, and its FTW_ variable: Configuration.
  • What to use where in production: a production stack.

docs.title: Background jobs
docs.text:
Let an agent start another agent and go on.

Let the chat start a researcher, and carry on talking while it works.

The chat is the assistant from Part 4, with one addition: a list of agents it may start in the background.

class IncidentAssistant(StreamingAgent):
    ...
    background_jobs: list[type] = [RootCauseResearcher]  # in assistant.py

The Session is yours: featherweight keeps no conversation, so a small class holds the history and wakes the chat when the researcher is done.

"""Chapter 5-3: a chat that starts a researcher in the background, and a session that wakes it when the note is ready."""

import asyncio
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from ag_ui.core import CustomEvent, TextMessageContentEvent
from assistant import IncidentAssistant
from langchain_core.messages import AIMessage, BaseMessage, HumanMessage
from terminal import read_line

from featherweight import AgentRunner, ChatInput, Database, SqliteDatabase, job_events


class Session:
    """The conversation, and the wake-up. featherweight keeps neither: this is yours to copy and change."""

    def __init__(self, db: Database, runner: AgentRunner, history: list[BaseMessage]):
        self.db, self.runner, self.history = db, runner, history
        self.turn = asyncio.Lock()  # one turn at a time
        self.watching: set[asyncio.Task] = set()

    def told(self, job_id: str) -> bool:
        """Has the conversation already got this child's result? A turn that was running when it finished is given it."""
        return any(f'job_id="{job_id}"' in str(m.content) for m in self.history)

    async def say(self, message: BaseMessage) -> None:
        async with self.turn:
            await self.run_turn(message)

    async def run_turn(self, message: BaseMessage) -> None:
        # the conversation is yours: the whole history goes in at each turn
        run = self.runner.stream(IncidentAssistant, ChatInput.from_langchain([*self.history, message]))
        async for event in run:
            if isinstance(event, TextMessageContentEvent):
                print(event.delta, end="", flush=True)
            elif isinstance(event, CustomEvent) and event.name == "background_started":
                task = asyncio.create_task(self.wake(event.value["job_id"]))  # follow the child
                self.watching.add(task)
                task.add_done_callback(self.watching.discard)
        print()
        self.history += [message, *run.new_messages]

    async def wake(self, job_id: str) -> None:
        async for _ in job_events(self.db, job_id):  # until the child's job is final
            pass
        print("\n[the researcher is done]")
        message = await self.runner.background_message(job_id)
        async with self.turn:  # after a turn that is running: what it was given is in the history by then
            if not self.told(job_id):
                await self.run_turn(message)  # the next turn, with its result


async def main(path: str = "reports/01-checkout-outage.txt") -> None:
    report = HumanMessage(Path(path).read_text())
    async with (
        SqliteDatabase(":memory:") as db,
        AgentRunner(db) as runner,
    ):  # in memory: a restart loses what is pending
        session = Session(db, runner, [report, AIMessage("I have the report. Ask me anything about it.")])
        while text := await read_line("\nyou> "):  # try: what was the root cause?
            await session.say(HumanMessage(text))
        for task in session.watching:
            task.cancel()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    try:
        asyncio.run(main(*sys.argv[1:2]))
    except (KeyboardInterrupt, EOFError):
        pass

you> what was the root cause?
I started the researcher; its note will come.
[the researcher is done]
The researcher says: something like the cause named in the note.

What to notice

  • background_jobs gives the model one more tool, start_background. It returns a job id at once, so the turn goes on. The researcher is an ordinary agent, run as a job of its own.
  • Results need a result store. The runner reads the researcher's note from it (the default sqlite store is enough here). An agent with background_jobs and no result store is refused before any model call.
  • The stream says what happened. The chat's stream carries background_started (with the child's job_id), which is how the session knows what to follow, and background_finished. The child's own job events are the full record: job_events follows them until the job is final.
  • runner.background_message(job_id) builds the user message with the child's result, and the session starts the next turn with it. A chat turn does not wait for its children.
  • Do not tell the model twice. A child that finishes while a turn is still running is given to that turn, and its message is in the turn's new_messages. So the session looks in its history first (told), after the running turn has ended, and starts a turn only for a result that the model has not had.
  • Here or on a worker is one line: AgentRunner(db, background=client) submits the researcher to a queue, and a worker that lists its job runs it.
  • Nothing is kept for you. If the process restarts, the history and the notes that were not stored are lost; this session keeps both in memory.

Why a message, not a tool result. The tool call already returned ("started"), and providers reject a second result for it. The result arrives as new information, as a user message. See background jobs and the guide.

Also possible

  • A chat that starts background work: the guide.
  • An agent that starts another and goes on, as a recipe.
  • Give the job what the parent knows: a context field in its input.

docs.text:
See what it did as OpenTelemetry traces.

Record the run as OpenTelemetry spans, and add a span of your own.

"""Chapter 5-4: the run as OpenTelemetry spans, with a span of your own. Collected in memory here, printed as a tree."""

import asyncio
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from incident import IncidentSummariser, Report, Summary
from opentelemetry import trace
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace import TracerProvider
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export import SimpleSpanProcessor
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export.in_memory_span_exporter import InMemorySpanExporter
from pydantic import BaseModel

from featherweight import AgentRunner, JobContext, OTelObserver, SqliteDatabase, job, run_job

exporter = InMemorySpanExporter()
provider = TracerProvider()
provider.add_span_processor(
    SimpleSpanProcessor(exporter)
)  # a real app exports to its backend: OTLP, Jaeger, a platform
trace.set_tracer_provider(provider)


class ReportFile(BaseModel):
    path: str


@job  # a class made from this function: a name, a version, a typed input and output
async def summarise_file(ctx: JobContext, input: ReportFile) -> Summary:
    with trace.get_tracer("incident_app").start_as_current_span("read the report"):  # your span, under the job's
        report = Report(text=Path(input.path).read_text())
    result = await ctx.run(IncidentSummariser, report)
    if result.output is None:
        raise RuntimeError(result.error)
    return result.output


async def main(path: str = "reports/01-checkout-outage.txt") -> None:
    async with SqliteDatabase(":memory:") as db:
        runner = AgentRunner(db, observers=[OTelObserver()])  # content stays off: capture_content=True turns it on
        await run_job(runner, summarise_file, ReportFile(path=path))
    depth: dict[int, int] = {}
    for span in sorted(exporter.get_finished_spans(), key=lambda s: s.start_time or 0):
        depth[span.context.span_id] = depth[span.parent.span_id] + 1 if span.parent else 0
        print("  " * depth[span.context.span_id] + span.name)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main(*sys.argv[1:2]))

invoke_workflow summarise_file
  read the report
  invoke_agent incident_summariser
    chat gemini-3.5-flash-lite

What to notice

  • OTelObserver is the observer that ships, and observers are classes: yours is Part 6. It goes on the runner. featherweight uses only the OpenTelemetry API: you configure the SDK and the exporter for your backend, as for any application (here an in-memory one, so that the book can print the tree; a real app exports with OTLP to its platform). Without an SDK it records nothing and costs nothing.
  • The spans follow the OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions, so platforms read them as they are:
What Span A job invoke_workflow {job} An attempt of an agent invoke_agent {agent} A model call chat {model} A tool call execute_tool {tool}
  • Your own span is under the job's, and the agent's attempts are siblings of it, because OTelObserver makes the job's span the current one while the job runs.
  • Content is off. The spans carry names, ids, status, tokens and timing, and no input, output or messages. OTelObserver(capture_content=True) (or OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_GENAI_CAPTURE_CONTENT=SPAN_ONLY) puts the content on the spans: it goes only where your exporter sends it, and featherweight keeps none of it.
  • Across the queue a submitted job and its worker form one trace: give the client the observer too, JobClient(db, queue, observers=[OTelObserver()]).
  • Evaluation is done on the traces you collect, on a platform of your choice. featherweight does not evaluate or score: it emits traces that carry the path (the model and tool calls, in order), which attempt counted (ftw.attempt.final) and the versions, so that a platform can.

Why an observer. It never changes a run: one that raises or is slow is logged and ignored. See observers and OpenTelemetry and the guide.

Also possible

  • Traces for jobs and agents, as a recipe.

Next: bring your own storage.

docs.title: Who is asking
docs.text: Book › Part 5: In production › Who is asking

docs.title: Who is asking
docs.text:
A tool that acts for the person who asked, and checks first.

Pass the identity of the run, and read it in a tool.

"""Chapter 5-5: who is asking. A tool that checks the identity of the run before it acts."""

import asyncio
import sys
from typing import ClassVar

from langchain.tools import ToolRuntime, tool
from pydantic import BaseModel

from featherweight import AgentBase, AgentInput, AgentOutput, AgentRunner, RunContext, SqliteDatabase

INCIDENTS = {"INC-7": ("payments", "Checkout is down for card payments."), "INC-9": ("search", "Search is slow.")}


class Responder(BaseModel):  # who the run is for: you define it, small, and no secrets
    user_id: str
    team: str


@tool
async def open_incident(incident_id: str, runtime: ToolRuntime[RunContext[Responder]]) -> str:
    """Open an incident by its id."""
    who = runtime.context.identity  # the model never sees this parameter, and cannot change it
    team, summary = INCIDENTS.get(incident_id, ("", ""))
    if who is None or team != who.team:  # featherweight carries the identity; checking it is the tool's job
        return "Not allowed."
    return summary


class Question(AgentInput):
    text: str


class Answer(AgentOutput):
    answer: str | None = None


class IncidentLookup(AgentBase):
    name: str = "incident_lookup"
    description: str = "Answers a question from the incidents the asker may open"
    version: str = "1"
    prompt: str = "Answer from the incidents you can open with your tool. If you cannot open one, say so."
    tools: list = [open_incident]
    input_model: ClassVar[type[AgentInput]] = Question
    output_model: ClassVar[type[AgentOutput]] = Answer


async def main(user_id: str = "ana", team: str = "payments") -> None:
    async with SqliteDatabase(":memory:") as db:
        runner = AgentRunner(db, identity_type=Responder)  # a declared type makes identity= required on every run
        result = await runner.run(
            IncidentLookup,
            Question(text="What is going on with INC-7?"),
            identity=Responder(user_id=user_id, team=team),
        )
        print(result.output.answer if result.output else result.error)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main(*sys.argv[1:3]))

Run it as ana (the payments team) and as raj (search): python app.py ana payments, python app.py raj search. The tool opens INC-7 for ana. For raj it returns Not allowed., and the model says it could not open it.

What to notice

  • The identity is a model you define, declared once on the runner (AgentRunner(db, identity_type=Responder)) and passed with identity=. A declared type makes identity= required, so one code path that forgets it cannot run a tool as nobody; Responder | None allows runs without one.
  • A tool reads it from its RunContext. The model never sees the parameter and cannot set it. If one agent serves different kinds of people (identity_type=Teacher | Student), the tool checks which kind it got before it acts. A launched agent and an agent started in the background have the identity of their parent.
  • featherweight carries it; you decide. Checking what the identity may do is the tool's job, and a refusal is text, as any failure of a tool is.
  • On a worker it is the same. client.submit(job, input, identity=...) puts it in the message with its kind, the name of its class, and JobWorker(..., identity_type=Responder) rebuilds it as that model (the guide). The runner must accept the worker's type, and a rename of the class while a job is queued fails that job.
  • It is a snapshot, taken when the job was submitted. A queued job can run later, after a role changed or a token expired: for a sensitive action, the tool re-checks with your application by user id. A tool gets a credential from the identity with your own code, at each call. The identity is small and has no secrets in it: it sits in the queue message.
  • A job is for one identity. If you pass a job_id to run yourself, pass the same identity every time: a run for another one raises. Resuming makes a new job, and reuses a step only for the same identity; whether someone may resume a job at all is your check.
  • A field that is not sent (exclude=True, for a value that exists only in your process) needs a default, because the worker rebuilds the identity without it. Do not change an identity after a run has it.
  • If you build agents from what users write, do not let them declare stdio MCP servers: they run commands on your server. Names of jobs are yours: unique in what your lookup searches, and stable.

Why carry and not enforce. Authentication, what a user may do and where credentials live differ in every application, so featherweight hands a typed identity to the tools and leaves the rest to you. See identity and the guide.

Also possible

  • A tool that gets a token for its identity.
  • Files are passed as references, not carried: files for an agent or a job.
  • An action that needs a person's yes: the agent proposes and your code acts, as in Approvals.

docs.title: Approvals
docs.text: Book › Part 5: In production › Approvals

docs.title: Approvals
docs.text:
An agent proposes, and your code acts after a person says yes.

An agent never books, pays or sends. It returns a proposal, a person approves it, and plain code executes it.

"""Chapter 5-6: approvals. An agent proposes, and plain code acts after a person says yes. Nothing here needs a model."""

import hashlib
import time

from pydantic import BaseModel

APPROVERS = {"ana"}  # yours: who may approve a rollback, from your own authentication
PROPOSALS: dict[str, dict] = {}  # yours: your database
DONE: dict[str, str] = {}  # idempotency key -> what was done


class Rollback(BaseModel):  # what the agent returns as its output: a proposal, not an action
    service: str
    to_version: str
    reason: str


def keep(proposal: Rollback, seconds: int = 1800) -> dict:
    """Stage one is over: keep the proposal with its hash and an expiry, and show it to a person."""
    shown = hashlib.sha256(proposal.model_dump_json().encode()).hexdigest()
    record = {"id": "p1", "proposal": proposal, "hash": shown, "expires": time.time() + seconds, "status": "pending"}
    PROPOSALS[record["id"]] = record
    return record


def approve(proposal_id: str, shown_hash: str, approver: str, key: str) -> str:
    """Stage two: plain code, with no model in it. It checks, then acts once."""
    if key in DONE:
        return DONE[key]  # the same approval again changes nothing
    record = PROPOSALS[proposal_id]
    if record["status"] != "pending" or time.time() > record["expires"]:
        raise PermissionError("it is not pending, or it has expired")
    if shown_hash != record["hash"]:
        raise PermissionError("it is not the proposal that was shown")
    if approver not in APPROVERS:
        raise PermissionError(f"{approver} may not approve")
    record["status"] = "approved"
    proposal = record["proposal"]
    DONE[key] = f"rolled {proposal.service} back to {proposal.to_version}"  # an API call, in real life
    return DONE[key]


def main() -> None:
    record = keep(Rollback(service="payment-form", to_version="4.1", reason="errors began with 4.2"))
    print("proposed:", record["proposal"].model_dump_json())
    for who, shown, key in [
        ("raj", record["hash"], "k0"),
        ("ana", "0" * 64, "k1"),
        ("ana", record["hash"], "k2"),
        ("ana", record["hash"], "k2"),
    ]:
        try:
            print(who, "->", approve(record["id"], shown, who, key))
        except PermissionError as exc:
            print(who, "-> refused:", exc)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

make book-chapter N=5-6

The proposal is shown, the wrong approver and a changed proposal are refused, and the right approval acts once, even when it is sent twice:

proposed: {"service":"payment-form","to_version":"4.1","reason":"errors began with 4.2"}
raj -> refused: raj may not approve
ana -> refused: it is not the proposal that was shown
ana -> rolled payment-form back to 4.1
ana -> rolled payment-form back to 4.1

What to notice

  • The agent has no tool that acts. Rollback is its output_model, and its allow-list holds read tools. A wrong answer, or a prompt injection, can only produce a wrong proposal. If it proposes in the middle of a conversation, give it a tool that only writes a proposal.
  • The proposal is data. It is typed, validated when the agent answers, kept by you with its hash and an expiry, and drawn on the screen from its fields. A sentence that the model wrote about it is decoration.
  • An approval is for exactly what was shown. The client sends the id, the choice and the hash it saw, never the arguments of the action. approve refuses a proposal that changed, expired or is not pending, and an approver who may not.
  • The executor has no model in it. It is plain code: an idempotency key makes a second approval change nothing. Revalidate what can have changed before you act (the slot is still free).
  • Only the streaming agent talks to the user. A sub-agent or a background job has its own tools, so it reads, and what it finds comes back to the streaming agent as a result, open_questions or a proposal.
  • A job asks at a boundary. Its agent ends with open_questions, the job succeeds with a typed outcome, you ask the person, and a new job with resume_from reuses the finished stage at no cost. Nothing is held while you wait.

Why not pause the run. A paused run needs its conversation kept somewhere, and a person may take a day. A proposal that is data can wait for as long as it must and holds nothing. What is left out, and when to think again, is in the approvals spec.

Also possible

  • Approving what an agent proposes: a flight search agent, a typed proposal, an executor, and a tool that proposes.
  • Asking the user in the middle of a job: two stages and resume_from.

Next: Part 6 shows how to plug in your own storage.

docs.title: Postgres
docs.text:
Switch the run log to Postgres.

The run log is a Database. SqliteDatabase is for local work and PostgresDatabase is for a deployment. They share one interface, so one line changes. The runner, the jobs and the agents do not.

The book's container starts no database and does not install the Postgres driver, so run this chapter in a venv on your machine:

pip install 'featherweight[postgres]'
docker run --rm -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=postgres -p 5432:5432 postgres:16-alpine
DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/postgres python 6-1/app.py

"""Chapter 6-1: the same run log, in Postgres. One line changes."""

import asyncio
import os

from featherweight import PostgresDatabase

DSN = os.environ.get("DATABASE_URL", "postgresql://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/postgres")


async def main() -> None:
    # Databases: SqliteDatabase (local), PostgresDatabase (a deployment), or your own (Chapter 6-4). The runner does not change.
    async with PostgresDatabase(DSN) as db:  # it was SqliteDatabase(...): the tables are made in a schema of their own
        job_id = await db.create_job("incident-report")  # a job id groups the runs of one piece of work
        job = await db.get_job(job_id)
        print(job.status.value if job else "no job")  # INIT


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())

INIT

docs.title: What to notice
docs.text:
• The databases are SqliteDatabase (local), PostgresDatabase (a deployment) and your own (a database).
  • The tables go in a schema of their own (featherweight by default), made by the same numbered migrations as in sqlite.
  • Two things stay sqlite: SqliteQueue and the default result store need the sqlite database. With Postgres, bring a queue (a job queue) and pass a result store (AgentRunner(db, results=...): a result store).

Why there is no Postgres result store: where results live is your decision, so featherweight asks you for one. See persistence.

docs.title: A result store
docs.text: Book › Part 6: Bring your own storage › A result store

docs.title: A result store
docs.text:
Keep the results of jobs where you want them.

A resumed job and client.result read results from a ResultStore. It has three methods: put, get and delete_job. The key is the job id, the hash of the agent or job, and the hash of the input; the output is a JSON dict.

The result stores are SqliteResultStore (the default: a table in the run log's file, for local work) and yours, over S3, Redis or a table:

"""Chapter 6-2: a result store of your own, checked with the kit. No model, no key."""

import asyncio
import json
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

from featherweight import ResultKey, ResultStore, testing


class FileResultStore(ResultStore):
    """One JSON file for each result, in a folder for each job. Stores: SqliteResultStore (the default, local) or yours: S3, Redis, a table."""

    def __init__(self, folder: Path):
        self.folder = folder

    def _file(self, key: ResultKey) -> Path:
        return self.folder / key.job_id / f"{key.agent_hash}-{key.input_hash}.json"

    async def put(self, key: ResultKey, output: dict) -> None:
        self._file(key).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self._file(key).write_text(json.dumps(output))

    async def get(self, key: ResultKey) -> dict | None:
        file = self._file(key)
        return json.loads(file.read_text()) if file.exists() else None

    async def delete_job(self, job_id: str) -> None:
        for file in (self.folder / job_id).glob("*.json"):
            file.unlink()


async def main() -> None:
    await testing.check_result_store(lambda: FileResultStore(Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())))  # raises if a rule is broken
    print("FileResultStore follows the ResultStore contract")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())

make book-chapter N=6-2
FileResultStore follows the ResultStore contract

It needs no model and no key. Use it with AgentRunner(db, results=FileResultStore(Path("results"))).

docs.title: What to notice
docs.text:
• testing.check_result_store takes a function that makes a fresh, empty store, and raises an AssertionError that names the rule your store breaks.
  • The store never sees featherweight's tables: it holds only the outputs you decided to keep.

Why featherweight keeps no results itself: they are your data, and how they are stored is your call. See the result store.

Also possible

  • A result store of your own, as a recipe.

docs.title: A job queue
docs.text: Book › Part 6: Bring your own storage › A job queue

docs.title: A job queue
docs.text:
Write a job queue over the queue you run.

A submitted job travels through a JobQueue. The queues are SqliteQueue (ours, for one machine), MemoryQueue (for tests) and yours, over SQS, a Redis stream or a table. The interface is five methods: enqueue, receive, ack, nack and extend.

The one rule that matters is the lease: a received message is yours for a while. If you do not ack, nack or extend it in time, it comes back with a higher delivery_count. That is how a message from a dead worker is delivered again. Real brokers already have it:

SQS Redis stream enqueue send_message XADD receive receive_message, with the lease as the visibility timeout XREADGROUP for new messages, XAUTOCLAIM for ones idle too long ack delete_message XACK extend change_message_visibility XCLAIM your own entry, which resets its idle time delivery_count ApproximateReceiveCount the delivery counter of XPENDING

This is a sketch. It is not run or tested here, because there is no SQS or Redis in this book or in its tests:

"""Chapter 6-3: a sketch of a job queue over SQS. It is not run or tested here: there is no SQS in this book's container.

Queues: SqliteQueue (ours, for one machine), MemoryQueue (for tests), or yours: SQS, a Redis stream, a table.
"""

from featherweight import Delivery, JobMessage, JobQueue


class SqsQueue(JobQueue):
    def __init__(self, client, url: str, lease: int = 60):
        self.client, self.url, self.lease = client, url, lease  # a boto3 SQS client, and the queue's URL

    async def enqueue(self, message: JobMessage) -> None:
        raise NotImplementedError  # send_message(MessageBody=message.model_dump_json())

    async def receive(self, timeout: float) -> Delivery | None:
        raise NotImplementedError  # receive_message(WaitTimeSeconds=..., VisibilityTimeout=self.lease): the lease is the visibility timeout
        # Delivery(message=..., token=<the receipt handle>, delivery_count=<ApproximateReceiveCount>)

    async def ack(self, delivery: Delivery) -> None:
        raise NotImplementedError  # delete_message(ReceiptHandle=delivery.token)

    async def nack(self, delivery: Delivery, *, requeue: bool) -> None:
        raise NotImplementedError  # requeue: change_message_visibility(..., 0); otherwise delete_message, or let the redrive policy dead-letter it

    async def extend(self, delivery: Delivery) -> None:
        raise NotImplementedError  # change_message_visibility(..., self.lease)

Check yours with the kit. It gives your factory a short lease, to see a message come back:

await testing.check_queue(lambda lease: SqsQueue(client, url, lease=int(lease)))

Why the lease is in the interface: a queue that loses a message when a worker dies would strand its job. See the queue and your own queue.

Also possible

  • A queue that signs its messages, as a recipe.

← A result store · Part 6: Bring your own storage · A database →

docs.title: A database
docs.text: Book › Part 6: Bring your own storage › A database

docs.title: A database
docs.text:
Put the run log in a store that featherweight does not ship.

This is an outline, and the biggest of the four. The databases are SqliteDatabase, PostgresDatabase and yours. Most people never need to write one.

  1. Read the schema. The tables, their columns and constraints are written down in the schema.
  2. Subclass Database and write its methods. They come in groups: connect and close; create, get and change a job; the compare-and-set steps that take, cancel, renew or take over a job; the events of a job; and the runs (create, mark running, finish, get, list, find one to reuse). Records go in and rows come out as Pydantic models, so a wrong type fails when the row is built.
  3. Mind the two hard rules. An event is written in the same transaction as the status change, and a compare-and-set step is one atomic statement, so that of a worker and a client exactly one wins.
  4. Check it with the kit. It gives you a fresh, empty and unopened database, opens and closes it itself, and names the rule that you break:
await testing.check_database(lambda: MyDatabase(dsn))

docs.title: What to notice
docs.text:
• Both ready-made databases pass this same kit. It is the contract, and the schema is the documentation.
  • If you only need the results somewhere else, you want a result store, not a database.

Why a Database is an abstract class with a kit: we cannot know your store, so we say exactly what it must do. See the database.

← A job queue · Part 6: Bring your own storage · An observer →

docs.title: An observer
docs.text: Book › Part 6: Bring your own storage › An observer

docs.title: An observer
docs.text:
Watch what a run does, and send it where you want.

An observer is a class that the runner calls as things happen: a job starts, an attempt ends, a model call finishes. The observers are OTelObserver (we ship it, observability) and yours. Every hook does nothing by default, so you override only the ones you need:

"""Chapter 6-5: an observer of your own, checked with the kit. No model, no key."""

import asyncio

from featherweight import ModelCallEnd, Observer, testing


class Tokens(Observer):  # observers: OTelObserver (we ship it), or yours
    """Counts the tokens of every model call. featherweight stores nothing that an observer receives."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.total = 0

    async def model_call_finished(self, call: ModelCallEnd) -> None:
        self.total += (call.input_tokens or 0) + (call.output_tokens or 0)


async def main() -> None:
    await testing.check_observer(lambda: Tokens())  # raises if a rule is broken
    print("Tokens follows the Observer contract")  # use it: AgentRunner(db, observers=[Tokens()])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())

make book-chapter N=6-5
Tokens follows the Observer contract

Use it with AgentRunner(db, observers=[Tokens()]).

docs.title: What to notice
docs.text:
• An observer always gets metadata (ids, status, tokens, timing). It gets content (messages, inputs, outputs) only if you set capture_content = True on the class.
  • An observer never changes a run: one that raises or is slow is logged and ignored. Calls are inline, so an observer that does slow work buffers for itself.

Why content is opt-in: the framework stores metadata and nothing else, and what leaves the process is your decision. See observers.
